To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the packet timing of a wide-area optical network is highly variable in both time and space, and that this behavior is caused in part by the presence of packet chains.

(1) packet-timing measurements can be performed on optical fiber with precision sufficient to capture the timing of individual packets, (2) packet-timing observations reveal that packet loss in wide-area networks occurs in bursts that are highly correlated with packet timing, and (3) packet loss can be explained in part by the formation of packet chains.
